parts.problem_md:

Complete the table with the name and function of each region.

| **Label** | **Name of the region** | **Function of the region** |

| **Q** |   |   |

parts.solution_md:
The completed table is as follows...

parts.problem_md:
Seizures in the brain can be investigated using different imaging techniques.

(i)  Which one of the following statements is correct?

**(1)**

☐ **A** CT scans are produced by the absorbance of magnetic fields 
☐ **B** CT scans are produced by the absorbance of radio waves by deoxyhaemoglobin 
☐ **C** CT scans produce a cross-sectional image of a thin slice through the body 
☐ **D** CT scans can be used to study brain activity while a person is undertaking tasks

(ii) During a seizure, part of the brain will be overactive.

Describe how positron emission tomography (PET) could be used to identify the part of the brain involved.

**(3)**
parts.solution_md:
(i) The correct answer is **C **because...

**CT scans produce a cross-sectional image of a thin slice through the body.**

> *A** and **B** are incorrect because CT scans use X-ray radiation, not magnetic fields or radio waves. MRI scans use those methods instead.*

> *D** is incorrect because functional MRI scans and PET scans can be used to detect which regions of the brain are being used during certain activities. *

(ii) Positron emission tomography (PET) could be used to identify the part of the brain involved in a seizure by...

Any **three **of the following:

- Isotope that emits positrons / is incorporated into glucose; **[1 mark]**
- More active neurones with increased respiration; **[1 mark]**
- Will require an increased supply of glucose; **[1 mark]**
- Positrons (emitted from glucose) produce gamma rays that detected and are converted into an image; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 4 marks]**

> *This question requires a high level of accuracy and detail. You should take some time to carefully review this topic in the revision page of our website and perhaps produce some flashcards on each of the methods of investigating the brain, or produce a graphic comparing the types to try and avoid confusion between them.*

parts.problem_md:
Some seizures can result in an increase in body temperature.

Suggest how a seizure in part of the brain could lead to an increase in body temperature.
parts.solution_md:
A seizure in part of the brain could lead to an increase in body temperature because...

- Impulses / electrical activity from the neurones at site of seizure; **[1 mark]**
- Arrive at / travel to the thermoregulatory centre in the hypothalamus; **[1 mark]**
- Description of consequence that would lead to increased body temperature eg. reduction of sweating / increased metabolic rate / increased respiration; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
The [scientific article](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2022/11/wbi15-01-que-20211021-scientific-extract.pdf) you have studied is adapted from *Rethinking Alzheimer’s* in *New Scientist *(February 2019).

Use the information from the scientific article and your own knowledge to answer the following questions.

Memory and cognitive function are two processes that occur in the brain (paragraphs 2 and 13).

Complete the table showing which parts of the brain are responsible for different functions.

All 4 correct cells: **[2 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
Some forms of dementia can be diagnosed using brain scans.

Compare and contrast the use of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and computed tomography (CT) scans to identify structures like plaques in the brain (paragraph 6).
parts.solution_md:
A comparison and contrast of the use of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and computed tomography (CT) scans to identify structures like plaques in the brain, as follows:

**Four** from the following, up to **two** for similarities, up to **two** for differences:

**Similarities**

- Both are (neuro-imaging) methods giving high resolution; **[1 mark]**
- Both give images of areas with plaques in the brain; **[1 mark]**

**Differences**

- fMRI is expensive / time-consuming **WHEREAS** CT is cheaper / quicker; **[1 mark]**
- fMRI will show metabolism / oxygen uptake / brain activity **WHEREAS** CT only shows structures; **[1 mark]**
- fMRI uses magnetic resonance **WHEREAS** CT uses X-rays; **[1 mark]**
- fMRI does not use ionising radiation **WHEREAS **CT does (so increased risk of cancer developing); **[1 mark]**

*Ignore fMRI has a higher resolution than CT*

**[Total: 4 marks]**

> *A common error that students should avoid is to describe fMRI and CT scans, rather than giving a real compare and contrast response, in which comparisons need to be written in the same sentence, not as separate paragraphs.*

parts.problem_md: Suggest how the amyloid protein may prevent bacterial infection in the brain (paragraphs 7 and 22).
parts.solution_md:
The amyloid protein may prevent bacterial infection in the brain (paragraphs 7 and 22) as follows:

Any** four** of the following:

- Amyloid protein will cause bacteria to stick together/agglutinate; **[1 mark]**
- Enhancing phagocytosis of the bacteria / stimulates activity of white blood cells<sup>1</sup>; **[1 mark]**
- Acts as an antibiotic / anti-microbial; **[1 mark]**
- Amyloid protein could disrupt ability of bacteria to adhere directly to host cell; **[1 mark]**
- Amyloid protein prevents the entry of bacteria into cells; **[1 mark]**

<sup>*1*</sup>*Accept a description of phagocytosis; do not accept 'triggers immune response'.*

**[Total: 4 marks]**

parts.problem_md: Explain how the bacterium *Porphyromonas gingivalis* that causes gum disease may invade the brain and cause inflammation in brain regions affected by Alzheimer’s disease (paragraphs 10, 20 and 21).
parts.solution_md:
The bacterium *Porphyromonas gingivalis* that causes gum disease may invade the brain and cause inflammation in brain regions affected by Alzheimer’s disease (paragraphs 10, 20 and 21) as follows:

Any** four** of the following:

- Bacteria are carried in the blood from (infected) gums; **[1 mark]**
- Bacteria penetrate the blood-brain barrier; **[1 mark]**
- Bacteria /bacterial products cause the release of histamine/chemicals/cytokines; **[1 mark]**
- Resulting in vasodilation; **[1 mark]**
- State a consequence of vasodilation eg. increased blood flow / oedema /increase in white blood cells in the brain/increased oxygen; **[1 mark]**

*Accept 'bacteria can invade white blood cells which cross the blood brain barrier'*

**[Total: 4 marks]**

> *Make sure to link your question back to the idea of **inflammation** in order to get full marks here!*

parts.problem_md: Suggest how gingipains may have a degrading effect on the memory of a person suffering from Alzheimer’s disease (paragraph 12).
parts.solution_md:
Gingipains may have a degrading effect on the memory of a person suffering from Alzheimer’s disease (paragraph 12) as follows:

Any** three** of the following:

- Gingipains are enzymes that break down proteins in membranes; **[1 mark]**
- Degrading/breaking down cell membranes **OR** they (permanently) open up transport channels in the membrane; **[1 mark]**
- Which results in loss of brain tissue in the cerebrum **OR** adversely affects the transmission of nerve impulses / action potentials in the cerebrum; **[1 mark]**
- Leading to a reduction in memory (especially short-term memory); **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
The team found genetic material from *P. gingivalis* in the cerebral cortex (paragraph 13).

Describe how the team could show that this genetic material is active.
parts.solution_md:
The genetic material from *P. gingivalis* in the cerebral cortex (paragraph 13) could be shown to be active by:

Any** three** of the following:

- The extraction of the infected part of the cerebral cortex; **[1 mark]**
- Use a microarray (to identify mRNAs in sample); **[1 mark]**
- (Analysis of mRNA) to identify genetic material from *P. gingivalis*; **[1 mark]**
- Use of bioinformatics / algorithms to analyse the (enormous quantity of) data (from the microarray); **[1 mark]**

*Accept 'the use of a specific microarray eg. an oligo-nucleotide microarray.*

**[Total: 3 marks]**

> *The key part of this question is how we know the genetic material is **active**. It is not sufficient to just analyse the bacterial **DNA** found in the cerebral cortex, as this will not tell us if it is actively being translated. Instead, the **mRNA** needs to be analysed! The bacterial mRNA will only be present if the bacterial DNA from **P. gingivalis** is actively being translated as mRNA is single-stranded and less stable than DNA, meaning it degrades more quickly.*
